notice: Epics are business or operational capabilities, never technical layers. Every requirement has exactly one primary epic, which owns it. A supporting mapping records a deliberate cross-cutting concern and never duplicates the obligation: the requirement is specified once, in its primary epic. Validation gates are derived from the member requirements by scripts/validate_specification.py and are deliberately not declared here, because a hand-written gate list cannot be kept true.
authority_note: This map implies no implementation order, estimate, delivery commitment, or authority. Readiness additionally requires everything listed in readiness_requires.

epics.title: Ordering and Pickup
epics.goal: A customer can place a pickup order through any channel and receive a feasible pickup commitment that Dopis then protects.
epics.supporting_rationale: Order admission is only meaningful against the shared capacity, hours, and stock rules owned by other epics, and the two customer tracking actions are bounded by the communications epic.

epics.title: Kitchen Operations
epics.goal: The kitchen reliably receives, acknowledges, prepares, and progresses every accepted order on a real tablet under real service conditions.
epics.supporting_rationale: The exception queue and the least-necessary-visibility rules are exercised inside the kitchen panel but are owned by the incidents and privacy epics.

epics.title: Capacity and Service Scheduling
epics.goal: Order admission reflects real kitchen workload, pickup windows, and service hours across every channel.
epics.supporting_rationale: Capacity is consumed by the ordering flow and surfaced in the kitchen queue; the values that parameterise it live in the pilot threshold register.

epics.title: Stock and Availability
epics.goal: Every channel sells only what physically exists, with auditable adjustments and safe availability control.
epics.supporting_rationale: Stock reservation and release are driven by the order lifecycle and by the Start preparation event; the opening checklist reviews stock but is owned by kitchen operations.

epics.title: Catalog Administration and Presentation
epics.goal: Jaime maintains a correct, bilingual, well-ordered menu without developer intervention, and historical orders remain intact.
epics.supporting_rationale: Publication approval and the safety-review rules constrain catalog administration but are owned by the food-safety epic, which is where their verification evidence lives.

epics.title: Allergen, Dietary, and Cross-Contact Safety
epics.goal: A customer never receives incorrect or incomplete allergen, dietary, or cross-contact information, and unsafe information stops sales immediately.
epics.supporting_rationale: Free-text notes, recommendation surfaces, and shared critical-ingredient controls can all invalidate a computed allergen result, so they are tracked here even though they are owned elsewhere.

epics.title: Bounded Upselling
epics.goal: Manually configured recommendations add value without blocking checkout, misleading the customer, or becoming an automated commercial engine.
epics.supporting_rationale: Recommendation eligibility depends on publication completeness and on the dietary recalculation owned by the food-safety epic.

epics.title: Customer Communications and Tracking
epics.goal: A guest customer can securely follow their order and receives the minimum operational messages, with no redundant or over-disclosing communication.
epics.supporting_rationale: The two permitted customer tracking actions and the SMS content limit are exercised here but owned by the ordering and privacy epics.

epics.title: Payment, Handover, and Shift Close
epics.goal: Payment at the premises, handover, and cash reconciliation are separate, correctable, and auditable events with an accountable close.
epics.supporting_rationale: Non-collection, third-party collection, and the pending-decision record all terminate at the handover and shift-close boundary.

epics.title: Incidents, Substitutions, and Recovery
epics.goal: Exceptional situations are visible, resolved within authorised limits, recorded without losing history, and escalated safely when they exceed shift authority.
epics.supporting_rationale: Every exception path in the ordering, stock, safety, payment, and pilot epics terminates in this queue and in this history.

epics.title: Responsibility, Access, and Attribution
epics.goal: Service runs only under an accountable responsible person, with bounded access, honest attribution, and owner-controlled permissions, and never without Jaime before delegation is formally confirmed.
epics.supporting_rationale: Authentication, mobile-backup limits, opening, close, and the reservation of permanent policy changes to Jaime are all expressions of the same authority model.

epics.title: Privacy and Compliance
epics.goal: Operational customer data is collected for a stated purpose, seen only where necessary, kept separate from marketing, and retained under approved rules.
epics.supporting_rationale: Data minimisation, the undecided in-person telephone rule, disclosure control, tracking-session lifetime, and the pilot minimum-controls obligation are privacy concerns owned by the epics that implement them.

epics.title: Pilot Governance, Calibration, and Reporting
epics.goal: The controlled rollout produces the evidence needed to calibrate operating values and to decide whether Dopis continues, without unsafe automatic or public progression.
epics.supporting_rationale: Channel origin, upselling measurement, report access control, and override recording are the data sources the pilot scorecard consumes, and the public-launch entry condition bounds how far controlled progression may go.
